# Independent audit: outer strict approximation and compatibility slack

Audited line by line:

* `candidate ff5285005955b0c7`;
* `candidate 39ba6f71d6fbae25`;
* the tube-measure dependency in Section 2 of `candidate 9854c663e6eb01b8`.


local-feasibility theorems, not an attained strict-class extremum or
an OC lower bound.

## 1. Outer approximation

For every direction u, the ball centered at -T_k u with radius
T_k+h_C(u)+1/k strictly contains C because

  [T_k+h_C(u)+1/k]^2
    -[T_k^2+2T_k h_C(u)+R^2]
  =2T_k/k+[h_C(u)+1/k]^2-R^2>0.

Its supporting halfspace in direction u is exactly
u.x<=h_C(u)+1/k. The included coordinate directions therefore give
one uniform compact ambient bound. The finite-net nearest-point
calculation correctly yields Hausdorff error at most (1+B+R)/k.
Finiteness of the ball intersection is essential and is present in
the proof of strict convexity and interior containment.

The uniform compact bound leaves finitely many possible integer bases.
An original empty slice is eventually empty; every nonempty slice is
contained in the corresponding approximate slice, and compactness
gives the reverse Hausdorff limit. This also applies to boundary-only
and lower-dimensional original slices. Pointwise indicator convergence
is valid because containment retains EVERY original point and positive
distance excludes every fixed point outside the closed limiting slice.

The mixed measure difference is nonnegative with mass delta_k, so its
uniform error on arbitrary measurable sets is exactly delta_k. The
normalized depth error bound delta_k/M_k follows with the displayed
algebra, including for points outside the support. For d=0 eventual
base stability proves literal equality of counting measures.

Upper semicontinuity of closed-halfspace depth uses outward parallel
enlargements and continuity from above, not a boundary-null assertion.
One convergent subsequence of centers, with eventually fixed integer
base, yields a single point of the original S. It is chosen before
any halfspace is tested.

## 2. Intrinsic diagonal

The vertical Minkowski tube has exactly the old nonempty base set.
On an r-dimensional compact convex fiber, the orthogonal decomposition
in the tube lemma gives the exact section
K+epsilon sqrt(1-|s|^2) B_r. Its rescaled weak limit is
kappa_(d-r) H_r|K, including r=0 and r=d. Scaling all fibers by
epsilon^(-(d-q)) retains only the q-dimensional ones, with their
common coefficient kappa_(d-q). The normalized total limit is positive.

At each epsilon_j the strictly convex outer approximation can be made
to have extra mixed mass at most epsilon_j times the tube mass and
Hausdorff error at most epsilon_j. Thus its NORMALIZED measure differs
from the tube measure by at most epsilon_j on every measurable set;
no comparison of unscaled masses with a vanishing limit is needed.
Hausdorff error to C is at most 2epsilon_j. Finally the Portmanteau
closed-set inequality on outward halfspace enlargements has the
correct direction and retains all intrinsic boundary mass. The
limiting constant is unchanged. For d=1 the geometric strict-fiber
facet-null premise remains false and is explicitly not asserted.

## 3. Independent fiber perturbations

For each target z, the representation polytope EXCLUDES its own
coefficient. Every nontrivial representation consequently combines
at least two distinct ambient points with distinct bases, and strict
ambient convexity puts the whole interpolant in int C. Thus a target
with a nonempty representation polytope is necessarily positive-volume.

Every extreme representation has a compact interpolant inside int K_z,
giving a positive inward distance. The minimum over finitely many
extreme representations is positive. The extension to all
representations uses the valid convex-set identity

  sum_p (sum_j alpha_j lambda_p^j) K_p
    =sum_j alpha_j (sum_p lambda_p^j K_p).

For perturbations of Hausdorff size epsilon, the source interpolant
moves by at most epsilon. Support-function inequalities imply
K_z eroded by epsilon B is contained in K'_z. Taking 2epsilon<delta_z
therefore proves EVERY source compatibility inclusion, not just the
finite extreme ones. Removing the target's own coefficient handles
all convex combinations and proves the exact integer fiber identity.
Zero-volume targets have empty representation polytopes and cannot
receive an unwanted interpolated fiber.

The equality conv(P) intersect Z^n=P uses the original convex projection
and is correct even if P has deficient affine rank. Perpendicular
base thickening adds no point in aff P and, for sufficiently small
radius, no other integer point in its bounded neighborhood. It thus
preserves all prescribed fibers exactly. One full continuous fiber
plus base spanning points gives the needed relative full dimension;
the perpendicular ball supplies the missing base directions.

The final realizing body need not stay strictly convex. Neither note
asserts that this local slack is uniform over approximants, or that
a minimizing body in the strictly convex class exists. Those missing
claims are not used in either proof.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
